nodes.summary: Let $b \le -7$ be an integer, let $S_{2,b}$ be the map sending an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits, and write $S_{2,b}^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate. For every finite set $A$ of positive integers there is an integer $k \ge 1$ such that $S_{2,b}^k(a) < 2b^2$ for every $a \in A$.
nodes.title: A common iterate of the negative-base digit-square map falls below twice the squared base

nodes.summary: Let $b \le -12$ be an even integer, let $S_{2,b}$ be the map sending an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits, and let $v$ be an integer with $0 < v < 2b^2$. Then there are integers $w$ and $c$ with $0 \le w < v$ and $0 \le c \le |b| - 2$ such that
nodes.title: A congruence for the negative-base digit-square map

nodes.summary: A natural number is happy when repeatedly replacing it by the sum of the squares of its decimal digits reaches $1$ after finitely many steps. Let $N_0 = 7899999999999959999999996$. The six consecutive integers $N_0, N_0 + 1, \dots, N_0 + 5$ are all happy, and every natural number $m$ such that $m, m + 1, \dots, m + 5$ are all happy satisfies $m \ge N_0$.
nodes.title: Smallest run of six consecutive happy numbers

nodes.summary: Let $b \le -4$ be an even integer. Then every finite set of positive integers is $(2, b)$-good.
nodes.title: Even bases at most $-4$ make every finite set of positive integers good

nodes.summary: Let $b \le -2$ be an integer, let $S_{2,b}$ be the map sending an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits, and let $I(t) = t + 1$. Let $T$ be a finite set of positive integers and let $F$ be a composition $F = f_1 \circ \dots \circ f_m$ with $m \ge 0$ (the empty composition being the identity), where each $f_i$ is $S_{2,b}$ or $I$. If the image $F(T)$ is $(2, b)$-good, then $T$ is $(2, b)$-good.
nodes.title: Goodness pulls back along compositions of the digit-square map and the successor map

nodes.summary: For an integer $b$, let $S_{2,b}$ be the base-$b$ digit-square map, which for $b \le -2$ sends an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits; write $S_{2,b}^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, and let $U_{2,b}$ be the set of positive integers $u$ with $S_{2,b}^m(u) = u$ for some $m \ge 1$. A finite set $T$ of integers is $(2, b)$-good if for each $u \in U_{2,b}$ there are integers $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$…
nodes.title: Good sets for the digit-square map

nodes.summary: Let $b \le -4$ be an even integer. For every natural number $N$ there is an integer $n$ such that $n + i$ is $b$-happy for every $0 \le i < N$.
nodes.title: Arbitrarily long runs of consecutive happy numbers in even bases at most $-4$

nodes.summary: Let $b \in \{-4, -6, -8, -10\}$. For every natural number $N$ there is an integer $n$ such that $n + i$ is $b$-happy for every $0 \le i < N$.
nodes.title: Arbitrarily long runs of consecutive happy numbers in bases $-4$, $-6$, $-8$, $-10$

nodes.summary: There is an integer $n$ such that $n + 2i$ is $(-3)$-happy for every natural number $i$, and an integer $a$ is $(-3)$-happy if and only if $a \equiv 1 \pmod 2$.
nodes.title: Happy numbers in base $-3$

nodes.summary: There is an integer $n$ such that $n + 3i$ is $(-2)$-happy for every natural number $i$, and an integer $a$ is $(-2)$-happy if and only if $a \equiv 1 \pmod 3$.
nodes.title: Happy numbers in base $-2$

nodes.summary: For every integer $b \le -2$, the integer $1$ is $b$-happy.
nodes.title: $1$ is happy in every negative base

nodes.summary: Let $b \le -3$ be an odd integer. For every natural number $N$ there is an integer $n$ such that $n + 2i$ is $b$-happy for every natural number $i < N$. Thus there are arbitrarily long finite arithmetic progressions with common difference $2$ of $b$-happy integers.
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions of happy numbers in odd negative bases

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be an integer and let $S_{2,b}$ be the base-$b$ digit-square sum, which for $b \le -2$ sends an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits. An integer $a$ is $b$-happy if $S_{2,b}^k(a) = 1$ for some $k \ge 1$, where $S_{2,b}^k$ denotes the $k$-th iterate of $S_{2,b}$.
nodes.title: Happy integers in a negative base

nodes.summary: For an integer $b$, let $S_{2,b}$ be the base-$b$ digit-square sum, which for $b \le -2$ sends an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits. Then $U_{2,b}$ is the set of positive integers $u$ such that $S_{2,b}^m(u) = u$ for some $m \ge 1$, that is, the positive integers lying on a cycle of $S_{2,b}$.
nodes.title: Cycles of the negative-base digit-square map

nodes.summary: For an integer $b$, define $T_b(f, a)$ for a natural number $f$ and an integer $a$ by recursion on $f$: $T_b(0, a) = 0$, $T_b(f + 1, 0) = 0$, and for $a \ne 0$, $T_b(f + 1, a) = r^2 + T_b(f, (a - r)/b)$, where $r = a \bmod b$ is the remainder of $a$ on division by $b$, with $0 \le r < |b|$ (for $b = 0$ one takes $r = a$ and $(a - r)/b = 0$). For $b \le -2$, $T_b(f, a)$ is thus the sum of the squares of the first…
nodes.title: Truncated digit-square sum in a negative base

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $d$ be integers with $0 < d < -b$, so that $b \le -2$ and $d$ is a nonzero base-$b$ digit. Then the base-$b$ digit-square sum $S_{2,b}$ satisfies $S_{2,b}(d) = d^2$.
nodes.title: The digit-square sum of a single digit

nodes.summary: Write $S_{2,b}$ for the base-$b$ digit-square sum, which sends an integer to the sum of the squares of its base-$b$ digits. Then $S_{2,-10}(-1) = 82$, $S_{2,-10}(10) = 82$ and $S_{2,-4}(5) = 11$. Indeed $-1 = 1 \cdot (-10) + 9$ and $10 = 1 \cdot (-10)^2 + 9 \cdot (-10) + 0$ have base-$(-10)$ digits $1, 9$ and $1, 9, 0$, and $5 = 1 \cdot (-4)^2 + 3 \cdot (-4) + 1$ has base-$(-4)$ digits $1, 3, 1$ (most significant…
nodes.title: Sample values of the negative-base digit-square sum

nodes.summary: For every integer $b$, the base-$b$ digit-square sum $S_{2,b}$ satisfies $S_{2,b}(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: The digit-square sum of zero

nodes.summary: Let $b \le -2$ be an integer. Every integer $a$ has an expansion $a = \sum_{i=0}^{n} a_i b^i$ with digits $0 \le a_i \le |b| - 1$, unique up to leading zero digits, and $S_{2,b}(a) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} a_i^2$ is the sum of the squares of these digits. The digits are produced from the least significant one by taking $a_0 = a \bmod b$ and passing to $(a - a_0)/b$, until $0$ is reached.
nodes.title: Sum of squared digits in a negative base

nodes.summary: For every integer $b \le -2$, $1 \in U_{2,b}$, where $U_{2,b}$ is the set of positive integers lying on a cycle of the base-$b$ digit-square sum $S_{2,b}$.
nodes.title: One lies on a cycle of the negative-base digit-square map

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
